title: What Is a Food-Contact Surface?
excerpt: A food-contact surface is equipment or utensil surface that normally touches food, or a surface from which food can drain, drip or splash into food or onto another food-contact surface.
content_html:
Food-contact surfaces are defined by how food can contact them, not only by whether food is intentionally placed on them. This classification matters because food-contact surfaces have tighter design, cleaning and sanitizing requirements than many surrounding surfaces.

FDA Food Code definition

The 2026 FDA Food Code defines a food-contact surface as a surface of equipment or a utensil that food normally contacts, or a surface from which food may drain, drip or splash into food or onto another surface that normally contacts food.

Common examples

  • Cutting boards and preparation tables.
  • Knives, tongs, spatulas and serving utensils.
  • Mixer bowls, blender jars and food-processing components.
  • Interior surfaces of food containers and pans.
  • Conveyor or chute surfaces that directly contact food.
  • Parts above exposed food where drips or splash can reach the food-contact zone.

Not every kitchen surface is food-contact

Floors, most walls, equipment exteriors and many handles are normally nonfood-contact surfaces. They still require cleaning, but the cleaning frequency and sanitizing requirements can differ.

Food-contact classification affects design

Under the FDA model code, multiuse food-contact surfaces should be smooth, free from breaks and crevices and accessible for cleaning and inspection. Damaged surfaces can trap soil and become difficult to clean effectively.

Food-contact surfaces must be clean

The 2026 FDA Food Code requires equipment food-contact surfaces and utensils to be clean to sight and touch and includes specific cleaning triggers when contamination may occur or food use changes.

Sanitizing follows cleaning

Under the FDA model code, utensils and equipment food-contact surfaces are sanitized before use after cleaning. The exact method depends on the approved hot-water or chemical sanitizing system and local adopted rules.

A practical classification test

Ask: Does food normally touch this surface, or can food or liquid drain, drip or splash from it into food or onto another food-contact surface? If yes, manage it as food-contact unless the applicable code or equipment design says otherwise.

Regulatory note

The FDA Food Code is a model code. Facilities should follow the food-safety requirements adopted by their own jurisdiction.

Practical takeaway

Food-contact surfaces include more than obvious preparation tables. Classification follows the path food can take, and that classification determines the cleaning, sanitizing and material-control expectations.

References

  1. U.S. FDA — FDA Food Code 2026, definitions and Chapter 4.
  2. U.S. FDA — Food Code 2026.
